items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then they called in the National Jazz Service Organization – Eunice Lockhart-Moss, myself, James Jordan – and asked us to give them some thoughts about how to make this a national organization.

ctx.x: Lester Bowie. We followed them through there, so we got to be pretty good friends. Muhal and I have remained very close friends, because Muhal was one of the founding members of the National Jazz Service Organization and then ultimately became one of the officers in that organization. So we stay in close touch. Then I was also – [I] sat as one of the judges at the Detroit Symphony Black Composers Competition, which Muhal won with a piece called Transversion. So we’re very close friends. At times we’re at odds,…
Can you put your activities in the avant garde in a time frame? When we lived with Charles in New York, that was ’78, ’79, but I know you’re talking about activities from a somewhat earlier time.
